trust_decision.summary: amf_data_clone trusts that a length-prefixed AMF string has no embedded NUL: it copies it with strdup (stops at the first NUL), then amf_string_new memcpy's the full declared size out of that shorter heap buffer (heap over-read; the strdup buffer also leaks).

landing_point.why: The summary names amf_string_new in amf.c. The real defect is in its caller amf_data_clone, src/amf.c:730, about 170 lines above in the same file.

fix_sites.entry_point: flvmeta --check (src/check.c:632-633) and update/inject with preserve-metadata (src/info.c:667); public lib API amf_data_clone (src/amf.h:144), recursing through amf_list_clone (src/amf.c:162)
public lib API amf_string_new; only the signature becomes const, no behavioural change

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No out-of-scope site exists. The only conceivable dismissal is that the info.c preserve-metadata route is an optional flag, but it goes through the same single function, so one fix covers it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Cloning must keep the full declared length, including embedded NULs, and must keep NULL/empty strings working (amf_str(NULL)). A fix that truncates to strlen would silently change preserved metadata and checker output.

O6_input_shapes: string with an embedded NUL before its declared length
string nested inside an object, associative array or strict array (cloned recursively via amf_list_clone)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Object/assoc-array readers re-create member names from a C string (amf_str + strlen); a variant that kept the wire length while copying from a NUL-terminated buffer would be the same mechanism.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same length-vs-C-string mix-up already exists at src/amf.c:340, src/amf.c:399 and src/amf.c:953; a maintainer optimising name copies could easily pass the wire size.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A metadata-merge helper that duplicates name strings with strdup and the AMF size, in the update path.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The merge code already moves names as char* (src/info.c:664); a 'deep copy name' helper there is plausible and sits in a different file from the AMF codec.

O9_family: memory safety: heap out-of-bounds read (length/terminator mismatch on copy)

O10_build.toolchain: CMake + C compiler (bundled libyaml in src/libyaml); tests use Unity
O10_build.project_tests: tests/check_amf.c has AMF string tests (test_amf_string_new, tests/check_amf.c:108-126); none cover clone with embedded NUL

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Use strlen/strnlen in amf_string_new or clamp size to the strdup'd length (truncates legitimate embedded-NUL strings), instead of passing the original buffer and size.

out_of_scope_notes: src/amf.c:1012-1014 amf_object_delete steps to the data node before comparing and dereferences it as a string (wrong node / possible NULL deref); a separate bug.
src/check.c:617,628,655-661 and src/check.c:776 compare AMF names with strcmp, so names with embedded NULs are compared truncated; this is a logic difference, not an overflow.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell); tiny_repo is inferred from the project being a small CLI plus bundled libyaml.
O1 counts the CLI routes (check, update/inject with preserve); other CLI commands calling amf_data_clone indirectly were not exhaustively traced beyond the grep of callers.
Whether the bug is still present upstream today: no latest release was provided.
